name: Euphoria sepulcralis
intro: I photographed an adult in the field. Published records document regional differences in its seasonal activity.

sections.title: Adults and larvae
sections.text: In Kentucky the species has an annual cycle. Pupation occurs in August, and adults are active from late summer into autumn and again the following spring. Florida records span more of the year. Adults visit exposed flowers. Larvae occur in soil beneath dead sod or manure.

distribution.caption: The map shows U.S. states with contributed photographs of this flower scarab. Its distribution also extends outside the mapped records.
distribution.alt: Documented regions for Euphoria sepulcralis: Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia.
